key_insight: OpenGEM26 expands molecular ML training data to 200,000 organic molecules and 4.4 million conformations, enabling a graph neural network force field (GPTFF-mol) that better captures energies, forces, and distorted geometries than prior models.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable surrogate for DFT in molecular simulation, especially for sulfur- and chlorine-containing organics where fast but reliable force predictions are needed.
method: Built OpenGEM26 from DFT optimization trajectories and non-equilibrium structures for H/C/N/O/S/Cl molecules with up to 10 heavy atoms.
Trained a graph neural network potential, GPTFF-mol, on ωB97X-D/Def2-SVP and Def2-TZVP data with dispersion corrections.
Benchmarked against QM9 coverage and ANI-2x, then validated on butane rotation and keto-enol tautomerization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 16 meV/molecule energy MAE (0.82 meV/atom), improved force prediction over ANI-2x, and broader coverage of energy, bond-length, and bond-angle space than QM9.
watch_item: The dataset is limited to molecules with up to ten heavy atoms and may not transfer directly to larger systems or chemistries outside H/C/N/O/S/Cl.
paper_title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields (GPTFF-mol) for Organic Molecules from Optimization Trajectories (OpenGEM26)
